■■■ My dearest friend,

  1. How painful your silence is to me! It only stirs up new imaginings in my poor mind, now picturing myself forgotten, now with a «who knows?» that I keep repeating; I cannot understand. She must be ill. If only I were not so heavily veiled2 by a very dense veil! It was woven by my sins and prevents me from seeing her who is part of my thoughts. Dear Adele, why deprive me until now3 of your news, when you had promised to let me have a letter from you for the Immaculate Conception?

  2. I assure you that on my return from Cento, where I had had to go4 because the Superior had caught smallpox, which was raging as an epidemic in this city, and especially in this City, where there were contagious cases [...].5

  3. I stayed there several days and witnessed horrible cases; on returning, I was sure a letter from you would be handed to me; seeing all the others, I asked whether by some mischance they had forgotten to include it with those they gave me; but no, alas, it was true that Adele had deprived me of one.

  4. How many things, my dear, I would have to tell you, especially about the House in Milan, which, for lack of very little means, I must wait to open.6 Dear Adele, remember Piacenza, for charity's sake, which, as you know, is the house of sorrows for me, and now even more so, since we are so many: forty-four people. Dear Adele of Jesus, turn a glance, a thought, to this very poor person, and you, who weigh everything so well, will understand what distress she is in who never fails each day to hold you close in the heart of Jesus; but I do not want to doubt your love in the least, just as I can assure you of the affection this most unworthy friend of yours has for you

Sr. Anna Maria Rosa Gattorno

She teaches her to meditate on the mystery of Jesus' incarnation, explaining the fruits that flow from it.

A.M.F.

Dear Francesca,

  1. I received your dear letter of the 17th; you tell me you wrote me another containing a little note from Caterina;1 that one I did not receive. My dear, I would like to write to you at length and send a couple of lines to my other dear Daughters too, but I am alone in writing, with no one to help me, and I assure you I have to stay up many nights to manage so many things; in particular I have had many very important letters to write. Today, though I spent what few moments I had at my desk, there is still work left for tonight.

  2. My dear, let us leave all these useless things and turn to what is useful for our souls, as the day of the great ineffable mystery of love approaches; he gives us everything so that we may feel, taste, learn to love and be nourished by this most living love,2 this delightful pledge who comes to us to teach us the way by which we must go to draw this savoury milk.

  3. Behold3 a God, such as he was, has made himself little and is nourished at a Mother's breast, having lowered his power purely out of love, reducing himself to the humblest and poorest of children. A mother, however poor, always finds somewhere to lay her newborn; and you, King of heaven and earth, had nothing but a handful of straw and a few cloths to wrap you in; for fire, in so dreadful a cold season, you were content with the warmth of the breath of two beasts which, revering you as their creator, stood meek and turned towards you in reverence.

Mother Rosa at her desk, in one of her characteristic poses.

4. Here, my dear, see how many points for meditation and reflection there are in the way our Good came to trace:

  • first, he left everything. So, he says, if you want to find me, you must leave all your affection, love and self-satisfaction, and simply drown yourself in a sea that can fulfil all your desires, a spring that will quench your thirst, however burning it may be.

  • Rich, because the riches I can give you, you could never possess, however powerful you might be on this earth of mud and misery.

  • But look at him: he has no clothes; so, to go to him and receive riches from him, one must be stripped, poor and naked; then he will clothe us in beautiful garments adorned with precious gems.

  1. My dear, it is very true that all these things are most distasteful to our human nature, because it feels stripped of its sensual pleasures and reduced to nothing in its sensible feelings; but what a consolation it would be for me when you keep yourselves annihilated in everything and seek only to please your Spouse Jesus4.

  2. Humility, you are the queen of every virtue!5 But, my dear Eternal Father, you will give this wretched creature, before she dies, the consolation of seeing this beautiful gem shine in these daughters of yours, in this house of glorious Saint Anne, grandmother of your Son Jesus; then indeed my head will rest happily on the pillow of death and, smiling at such consolation, will remain with you for eternity.

  3. So, my daughter, ah! courage to fight well against the sad powers of the senses and the flesh, to will at all costs that our spirit always be victorious in us, and to try to respond to every inspiration our Jesus never ceases to give us and so often makes us feel forcefully;6 while we reject them with the greatest indifference, as if they were nothing; and yet one day we shall be asked to give a strict account of them. Woe to the creature who has turned a deaf ear to the inspirations God in his mercy gives her!

Goodbye; the Lord bless you, and believe me your most loving Mother Rosa

8. P.S. Greet everyone for me and tell them I will never stop praying for them all, that dear Jesus may come down into their hearts. I would like you to get Gigino's underwear and stockings7 to Papa's house, if there is still time before his brother goes to Savona; and also

I hope you have finished the slippers for Giustina;8 wrap them in a nice sheet of paper with the watch-holder and send them to my sister, for Carlotta is very anxious, fearing that you have not finished the work.

9. Without showing him this scrawl, ask Fr. Ricchini to have the pasta factory send me 5 «pesi» of the pasta we call «avvantaggiata» and two of the fine kind with saffron; I would like it at once; they can send me the bill, or he can give it to you, and I will get you the money to pay it.

10. I enclose the envelope with the letter to give to poor Angiola, a little note I am adding for her, sure she will take it well. I am already sure she will not let her virtue be overcome and will bravely make an offering of it to the Lord.

If you want to go and see the Crib at the Capuchins in Genoa, you can take the omnibus early in the morning and go with the good Caterina and Maddalena;9 but make sure it is very early, because later you would find too many people. Two of you should stay at home, so you will go two at a time. Say an Our Father for me to Saint Anthony, and five to Saint Francis (two beautiful altars), for my intention.

11. After New Year's Day I will be with you. Tell Fr. Ricchini, and greet for me our two dear good friends Maddalena and Caterina. I am not sending you anything, because you are in a city where there is everything.

Another evening I will send you a letter to give secretly to Caterina Rapallino, who will come to see you in a few days. Tell her to stand firm,10 and if her mother would leave her with you for a few days, you would do well to keep her. I hope they will have put up the paper partition before she comes. I hope you have got everything ready to take in the girls at risk and begin the work.

My dear, for ever mine, beloved daughter Caterina,1

  1. If the days were in my power I would certainly make them fly, so that my Caterina might soon come to me; but what lovely thoughts! Now tell me, my dear, whether these are illusions, or whether one day I shall have the good fortune to see them come true?2

  2. Caterina, you tell me to leave you in peace, because you always feel something calling you. Ah, my little daughter, that is not me but your spouse, who, poor thing, is dying of jealousy for fear that Caterina will betray him; and besides, should this voice not make itself heard?3

  3. Now more than ever, because in a few days the dear Child is coming and wants to find hearts empty, for he longs to enter them and rest; and shall we refuse to give him a heart for himself?4 Ah, it is indeed nothing compared with the Being who comes to dwell in it! The very thought exalts us and makes us too, poor creatures, God's; better said, God in the creature: we become one with the Creator.5

  4. To reach this,6 you see, dear Jesus is a Child; so he wants us to become children and grow only in him, and he wants to grow in us, giving us his food and strengthening us with the precious wine of his Blood. He wants us to live on this in this life, so as then to come into his presence in the purple robe enamelled with his most divine Blood.

  5. My daughter, we cannot have this purple unless we climb onto the Cross. He, God, left it on this holy Wood, the bridal bed of his most beloved spouses.7

6. I would like to tell you a thousand things and speak to you a little of this dear love. Dear daughter, love, for charity's sake,8 and keep all your love for this Being, taking nothing from him. Everything for him, yes, yes, everything. I close, leaving you in the Heart of Jesus, a delightful dwelling, where I hold you with all my strength, and I would like one day to see you melted in it.9

Goodbye; I am yours for ever, your poor Mother

Sr. A. M. Rosa

7. P.S. Burn this letter at once so that they cannot find it on you; I would be too sorry. The Superior asks me to tell you she will write to you, and so will Carlottina, who has no time now. The Superior, Eufemia and Carlotta send their greetings.10 Keep the promise you made her.

  4. Goodbye, my dear. You will find a little basket containing a cloth jacket for the teacher,4 and a small boy's shoe, which will serve as a measure for you to buy a pair of woollen ones, but with leather outside and only the wool inside. This shoe should fit inside those you buy; better that they be larger; and send them to me at once with the chocolate. Tell Ricchini too that the uniform is being woven here, and I cannot understand why he has not sent me the pasta;5 if need be you can have it sent, that is, ordered through Angiolina,6 only the «avvantaggiata» and one «peso» of the fine kind.7 Six of «avvantaggiata» and one of fine, with the bill, so that I can send the money order to the seller himself; and once the way is open we will go on buying from him, if it suits us.8

Goodbye; I will write again on Saturday.

I am your most loving Mother. God bless you

Various instructions. She will come to Sampierdarena as soon as possible.

A.M.F.

Dear daughter,

  1. It is late, and with my face bandaged because I have caught a chill, I am writing two lines to urge you to keep the timetable and the Rules.

  2. Then, my dear, do not be so upset by what people say.1 Let us thank the Lord, who gives us the chance to gain merit by practising patience.

  3. I enclose a letter for Signora Morando;2 do not send it to her; wait until she comes, or else send for her. Never again say that I do not want to come unless there are keys to another house.3 Silence, because that is what pleases the Lord.

  4. I am sorry that the other day I wrote that I was sending you 30 francs and then forgot, and the address where to collect the money too;4 but I will send it in another letter. If you need money, write and tell me, and I will send it at once.

  5. I am tied down here as never before, but I will come as soon as I can. You see, I did not even go to Parma,5 because I want to finish there in Sampierdarena first. Tell everyone: Mother will soon be here, for that is my intention; and tell them too that I have caught this chill, but it is a slight thing that I hope will soon pass, for it is very cold here: the water freezes in the glasses, and in the basins in the bedrooms.

  6. I close, as it is late. If you have not yet sent the things, add mamma's rug.

Goodbye. The Lord bless you, and all of you.

I am your most loving Mother

She will send the community the money it needs little by little. Advice and exhortations.

A.M.F.

Dear Francesca,

  1. I received your dear letter; you are right, I was a goose,1 for I completely forgot the money; now I plan to send it to you little by little, five francs at a time.

  2. I have also replied to Signora Morando; for now there is no point in her coming; everything in its time, and sooner than you think. Let people talk; you just try to be very exact in keeping your Rules and the timetable. As soon as I can2 I will be with you. I also enclose two lines for the teacher.3 And be cheerful, without worries: with trust in the Lord everything is obtained.

  3. I cannot go on, because I feel really ill.

I am your most loving; God bless you, and I am your loving Mother

A strange illness of Carlotta's. A rebuke to two Sisters.

A.M.F.

Dear Francesca,

  1. Your reproaches would be just if things were as you imagine, but unfortunately they are different. Since I arrived in Piacenza this donkey1 has had no rest day or night: nights for accounts and letters, days for work, for our loom workshop gives me no small amount of work and care.2

  2. And now, to crown it all, my God! Carlotta fell ill a week ago with a very strange and frightening illness. My dear, she is as if mad, and neither your [sister] nor I can leave her bedside. Angiola too. Often, when she is raging, not even four of us can hold her: she punches everyone. My Jesus, I assure you this draught is very bitter for this poor mother! The doctor assures me that she will return to normal3 and that it is not madness, but first he had us apply leeches, saying it was a congestion of blood in the brain; now he says «nervous irritation», but dear Carlottina does not get better. Prayers, candles. On Sunday she was so violent that the Father had to stay the night.4 What do you think of that? It is very late now and she has been resting for two hours, crying out now and then. Last night the Father stayed again, and I had to be at her bedside the whole time, her fury was so great; your sister too.

  3. I feel ill; the vomiting is killing me. I cannot take anything. That is my wretched situation. Blessed be the Lord for ever!

  4. I hoped to be with you on the first day of Lent;

now I say nothing more. As soon as I can leave Carlotta or bring her, I will come. She is suffering immensely. I close.

  1. Read these few words to these stubborn Daughters, unworthy to bear the name of Daughters of Saint Anne. Sister Serafina, how often I urged you, telling you that one must work and that holiness consists in obedience and not in eating.5 I mean this for all of you, and especially for Sister Serafina and Addolorata.6 Your abstinences do you no good: ashes for hell. Now is the time to work, and you have no strength. On the day of judgement they will see whether this creature told them the truth. I tell you that if you do not change, when I come I shall be obliged to take the measures our holy Rules require of me.

  2. I assure you, my dear Superior, that I feel your sorrow and distress over these stubborn Daughters so much in myself that it grieves me. Dear Jesus, this is truly painful to me, because I know it displeases you. The rest I will discuss when I come. My greetings to those two, and to dear Carolina. Read it as best you can, for I am writing in haste on a corner7 of the table.

God bless you; and you, have faith in the oil.8 Anoint yourself often, and I hope you will soon be healed, and dear Jesus, passing by, will heal you with his little hand. Pray to him.

[your most loving Mother Rosa]

She informs her of her forthcoming arrival at Sampierdarena.

A.M.F.

Dearest in Jesus,

  1. I let you know that next Sunday1 I shall be at Sampierdarena. I hope you will honour me with a visit, for I long to see you together with those blessed creatures.2

  2. I am sure you will not deprive me of so great a favour, though I am unworthy, being so infamous. Goodbye; I will tell you many things in person, and I will bring you something I know you will like very much.

Greet the dear creatures for me and pray for me.

I am your most affectionate friend, Sr. Anna Maria Rosa

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc31:
Fr. Luigi Cogrossi had known M. Rosa before the foundation, had advised her to begin her work in Piacenza and then helped her at the Mother House for about a year (1866-67), acting as director. Cf. Letter 2, n. 6; 3, n. 3.

Piacenza. The first band.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc32: She had met Rosa Gattorno in Genoa and was staying at the Mother House for health reasons. Suffering from bronchial asthma, she had been entrusted by her parents to M. Rosa in the hope that the climate would help her. She showed signs of a vocation but had not yet asked her parents' permission. She would take the habit of the Daughters of Saint Anne on 8 December 1869 with the name Sr. A. Vincenza.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc34:
The Mother had arrived with the sisters only 16 days before. The chronic disorganisation of the hospital in Cento was notorious, and various attempts to remedy the «indiscipline and immorality of the staff serving in the wards» had been almost fruitless. Cf. L'Ospedale di Cento nei secoli, ed. Cassa di Risparmio di Cento, 1975, p. 209ff.

She was training those willing young women in the tasks entrusted to them, namely the general services of kitchen and linen room and the nursing of the women's ward. Given the situation, tact, patience, time and much spirit of sacrifice were needed.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc35: Patience and sacrifice, outstanding features of Rosa Gattorno's strong spirituality.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc36: Love is expressed not so much in words as in deeds. This is the teaching of the life of Jesus, marked by the paschal mystery.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc37: Looking to Christ, acting as grown women in him, offering oneself to the Father with resolve and abandonment to his will.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc38: Only the awareness of being loved and chosen gives rise to a courageous response, unsettled and on the move, like that of the apostles.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc39: The style is vivid, suited to the young women Rosa was initiating into religious life. Noteworthy is the strong dynamism of discipleship in the verbs of movement and the demands of discipleship: availability, resolve, poverty.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc40: Suffering was their refreshment. The expression is frequent in Mother Rosa's ascetical and mystical language. From «suffering» with Christ there sprang up in her spirit joy and an expansion of vital strength.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc41: Here is the synthesis of Rosa Gattorno's spiritual doctrine: accepting the cross as Jesus' gift and carrying it with Jesus, in a relationship of poverty and weakness that lets itself be enriched and «made beautiful» by the Spouse, so as to make us pleasing to the Father.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc42: Teresa Porta. Cf. letter of Luigia Ferro and letter of Maria Pizzo, Teresa's mother, to whom her daughter had gone, with M. Rosa's consent, to nurse her. Arch St FSA, Pos Amiche.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc43: A very dense conclusion. The one reason for each one's being and acting: Christ.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc44: Angela Degrossi, another of Mother Rosa's first five followers.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc45: Past midnight... cutting short her night's rest in order to write to her daughters would be a dear habit all her life.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc46: The spiritual advice and norms of religious life are sober, essential and clear, eminently practical and concrete: sure tracks on the way to holiness.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc47: Expressions of motherly tenderness and warm humanity, of affectionate reciprocity.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc48: Her concern for the sisters is personal, attentive to each one. Angela Degrossi, cf. Letter 7, n. 12; Rosa Podestà, one of the first five who received the religious habit on 8 December 1866.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc52: She had kept this letter aside so as to be able to reply.

This is the first of the 116 letters in this collection from Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, one of her first collaborators. Cf. Index II, 3.

This letter, however, though addressed to her, is for all the sisters in Cento.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc63: A terse remark alluding to the continual, varied and recurring difficulties of the community at Cento.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc64: To check during the night whether it had gone out and relight it. The advice that follows on this point reflects great experience and prudence.

The habits... the religious habit the young women would put on at a special ceremony presided over by Father Tornatore. Cf. Letter 15, n. 6.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc71:
Saint Anne's presence already has notable charismatic significance, marking the being and acting of the Daughters.

Such relish is a gift of Jesus. He draws a balmy ether from thorns. The Mother's language, typical of the mystics, reveals her experiential knowledge of living Christ, the Crucified, her Good.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc78: Such a gift is not the exclusive privilege of a few. Let them ask for it and beloved Jesus will grant it.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc80: Besides strengthening unity and communion, frequent correspondence was necessary to keep her informed about daily life and events, which were full of unpleasant conflicts.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc84: Motherly solicitude and watchful attention to everything that could foster the physical and spiritual health of the sisters, all very young, engaged in the heavy general services (kitchen, linen room) of the hospital and in nursing the sick, and so exposed also to the danger of infection.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc85: The girls, that is, the sisters. A very important recommendation. Joy and serenity are needed in order to grow in the spiritual life and devote oneself to the service of charity. But in difficult situations attention must be redoubled, so that zeal is not broken by sadness; Mother Rosa wanted sadness wholly banished from her daughters' hearts and never tired of urging them to be cheerful.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc86: The expression signifies the soul and style of the Daughters of Saint Anne's «service» to the sick.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc87: Fr. Michele Vaccari, confessor of the religious community. Cf. letter of Francesca Camisa, 11.7.1867.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc89: The tone is confidential, the style that of a dialogue, the content centred on the core of the Mother's spiritual teaching: love of the Cross. «You know what lies in suffering, don't you?» An expression that gives lift, resolve and courage more than a long speech.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc90: Over time the figure of Saint Anne takes on affective and spiritual colouring.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc92: She does not hide her own financial straits. She had taken in the cholera orphans at the Mother House.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc93: Caution in writing. Letters were tampered with and checked; hence the Mother's fears, which were certainly not unfounded.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc94: Fr. Tornatore's influence was growing. He was already regarded as the spiritual father of the community; first Father, certainly in relation to Fr. Luigi Cogrossi, Director of the Work. The young women who made up the community, including the superior, had not yet received the religious habit, for two reasons: the climate in the hospital was unfavourable to religious, so that the Concettini had presented themselves as a lay association in civilian dress; and the Institute, moreover, was only just beginning. Nor did the Church yet have a canonical procedure with precise norms for Institutes of active life; these were in fact approved by the Sacred Congregation of Bishops and Regulars with the document «Secundum quas» in 1901. The Rule of the Institute provided for two months of postulancy before clothing and three years of probation, after which profession of temporary religious vows was made. Arch St FSA B. 1. 61.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc96: With severity and firmness the Mother cuts short mistaken ideas about true virtue. Holiness does not consist in arbitrary fasting but in obedience. The superior is to help the young woman discern where her penitential choices come from.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc100: The postulants had asked the Mother to write a prayer for them.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc103: Eucharistic adoration at the Mother House was frequent.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc105: The wife of the hospital's head physician, Signora Irene Fortini Facchini. M. Rosa corresponded with her; cf. Arch St FSA, Posiz. Cento.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc106: Carlotta was at the Royal Institute for the Deaf and Dumb in Milan.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc108: Caterina Rapallino suffered from bronchial asthma, so the remedy did her harm, making it hard for her to breathe.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc109: The Spiritual Exercises, in preparation for the feast of Saint Anne, the taking and renewal of Vows and the «clothing» (entry into the Novitiate).
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc110: She had decided that on that day some of them would receive the religious habit.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc112: The eschatological dimension is very strong in Mother Rosa. She expresses it often in her letters, with varying emphases and nuances.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc113: The charism of Saint Anne's presence is taking shape in that charity which becomes human closeness, a mother's love that takes on the suffering of those one loves and serves.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc114: Mother Rosa meditated assiduously on Christ's passion and had prescribed it for her daughters too.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc115: The religious services for the feast of Saint Anne were celebrated solemnly from the very beginning.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc116: The letter she mentions is missing. Cf. Letter 15, 3. It is a matter of justice as well as sound administrative practice.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc119: Annunciata Chiodelli. Having fallen seriously ill, she recovered through the Mother's prayers. Cf. Fiocchi, op. cit. I, p. 177 ff.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc122: The formal «lei» used by the Mother is surprising; she certainly adopted it to conform to the norms of religious life given to the Sisters by Fr. Tornatore.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc123: The mirror. A symbolic image expressing the intentional relationship with Christ, the aspiration to reflect in one's own conscience his reality and sublime holiness, «his model». His perfection is reflected in us and transforms us; «it makes us beautiful», she says elsewhere.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc124: Here is the programme nourished by charity: contemplation and action; motherly welcome and self-giving, like Saint Anne.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc125: Speaking of charity recalls her mystical experience of the «fire» that kindled in her an insatiable «longing» for God and love for her brothers and sisters.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc126: If the letter had not been posted that same morning it would have arrived late, disappointing the Sister, who was waiting for it.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc128:

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc155:
Yes, you are my treasure. She is addressing «suffering» directly.

She asks Jesus to give all the suffering to her and relieve her daughters, still little, unable to find «joy» in it. Suffering is her only treasure: she has discovered it, loves it, and it belongs to her.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc163: Olive oil which she had blessed following an inspiration received in prayer.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc164: She tactfully and gently repeats the advice of Letter 15.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc166: She wants to replace her personally. She is bringing Caterina Rapallino, the young woman who is discerning her own call to the Daughters of Saint Anne and is strongly opposed by her parents.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc167: The burdens of the Piacenza house were enormous; consider only the debt to be repaid to Teresa Porta. Cf. Letters 31, 32, 33.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc168: Humility! She never tires of instilling it. Here we hear an echo of the «perfect joy» of her «dear Father Saint Francis», whom she had followed as a tertiary, making her profession on 24.9.1861.

Siili fi Piacenza. Mother House. The façade.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc178: Another reassuring word and an invitation to meet again in prayer before him who is the centre of unity and the source of peace.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc183: From their arrival the people had appreciated the new institution of the «Genoese ladies».

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc188: The P.S., as an additional recommendation, is a note of special attention and motherly affection towards all her «dear Daughters».
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc189: The expressions about Saint Anne repeat Fr. Tornatore word for word: «great Woman... great Saint».
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc190: She points out the inconsistency: «if things are going well», why «is it necessary for me to come a little sooner?».
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc191: My daughter, show yourself a daughter of Saint Anne. Here is her face: generous, detached, seeking only the interest, pleasure and glory of the holy Mother; ready to stay or go anywhere and to suffer everything for Jesus.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc196: 4 October, feast of Saint Francis of Assisi.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc197: True absorption: the mystical experience of feeling deep within the transforming touch of his presence.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc198: Closeness, being united in Christ's love, is a source of consolation.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc200: Whether I am coming or going: with so many mouths to feed (cf. Letters 36, 6 and 38, 5), debts were piling up and suppliers were demanding payment.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc201: They thus lived in extreme poverty, trusting in Providence and praying that it would not turn very cold.

Eliseo Ghislandi, director of the «Royal Institute for the Deaf and Dumb», where Mother Rosa's daughter Carlotta was a pupil, was working to found a work for deaf-mute girls «already educated» in other Institutes and sent back by them to their families. He was in negotiations with Mother Rosa.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc213: Neckbands: part of the Sisters' habit, to which the collar was sewn.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc214: Carlotta was still in Piacenza with the Mother. (Cf. Letters 14, n. 2; 18, 2; 19, 6, etc.).

Cf. Index III, 1.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc236: A few words, but full of human and spiritual force. They vividly reveal Mother Rosa's personality and her motherly feeling and understanding.

Clearly the sisters too were caught up in this very critical situation.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc354: The Mother draws her daughter into her own path of following her Crucified Good. Adversities and daily sorrows are the nails of our crucifixion, so we must look on them as instruments that help us express our love for Jesus (cf. Gal 2:20).

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc358: She is ready, as always, to take on the young woman's distress, but she cannot heal her state of mind: the young woman must herself make the effort to come out of her sadness.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc360: It is the behaviour of foolish people who go by worldly conventions and customs.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc363: Advice dictated by prudence, which demands respect for the secrets of the heart.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc364: The young woman is going through a crisis because of her poor health. The Mother tirelessly continues to apply her vocational pedagogy. The only way out of this painful state is to let herself be loved by Jesus, the only love, and to follow him, won over by his love.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc365: By following Jesus she will also understand the Mother's love: she seeks only her good, an infinite good. Then she will be able to overcome every emotional tie and give herself freely to Jesus.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc366: In these expressions M. Rosa condenses her own spiritual experience of total self-giving to Christ. She had noted in her Memoirs: «...I feel no desire for anything; I live wholly in my God, yet I do not live, because I am always grafted into my Beloved» (M 1. 1, 111-112). Cf. Rom 8:11-13.

If they came to know me and saw who I really am, they would flee from me and their eagerness would turn to contempt.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc372: Patience is needed. In her littleness she feels she is nothing, a wretched creature, a sinner, and entrusts herself to God's mercy.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc373: The content of the letter the Mother is answering can be inferred from her words, as the letter itself has not survived. The Superior was complaining about the community's poverty and hardship, and the Mother attributed the lack of help from «providence» to «her own sins», with a humility that can only be understood in the light of contemplating Christ Crucified, humbled to the utmost abjection. And she, Foundress and Superior General, goes so far as to thank God for having removed her from the Mother House. Her daughters will receive light directly from the holy Mother Saint Anne to keep the holy book of the Rules.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc374: She entrusts herself to her daughters' prayers. To what the superior has said she opposes no judgement against her and no justification of herself. She takes on the wrong, lives the contradiction, and strives to resolve it in fidelity to her God.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc375: Fr. Angelo Ricchini was the priest who invited her to open a work to shelter girls at risk and a school for the young people left to themselves on the city streets. Cf. Index III, 3.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc376: At that time she evidently could tolerate no food but bread, and she was ashamed of it as a peculiarity that drew attention and made people suppose it was a penance.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc377: Humility is truth and does the truth. So to what has been imputed to her as a fault she replies calmly and peacefully, with the reason dictated by her conscience: and yet, my dear, I can assure you. Nothing but charity moved her in what she did.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc378: The five sisters of the community (whose superior is Sr. A. Francesca Camisa), good, docile and exemplary, deserve the marks of affection that she, though frank and rough in character, knows how to give. But their behaviour towards her also sharpens her sense of unworthiness.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc390: A typically motherly psychological delicacy, aimed at fostering harmonious and complete growth to full stature in the charismatic identity of a Daughter of Saint Anne.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc395: Her interpretation of the trial: it is a precious means of giving the Lord tangible proof of love and strengthening one's resolve to follow him radically and totally.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc396: Mother Rosa always has in view the whole of God's plan for the lives of those «called», the historical and eschatological dimension of human life.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc409: She has sinned and must pay the consequences. But stronger than her sin is the love of her God, who presses his blessed hand on her back with an intention of mercy.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc410: This teaching shines with the spirit of the beatitudes: «rejoice and be glad» (Mt 5:12); «I am overflowing with joy in all our affliction» (2 Cor 7:4); «affliction produces endurance, endurance proven character, and proven character hope» (Rom 5:3-4).
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc411: This is the only way: through life's trials accepted in faith and patience we grow in the capacity to love, even to love those who offend us. Cf. Lk 6:27-28.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc412: The many enemies oppose, persecute, speak ill. Was this not the lot of Jesus? And is his promise not true: «great is your reward in heaven»? Her daughter will have to reach this goal gradually, freeing herself from purely human and psychological considerations.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc413: Prudence and discretion, indispensable virtues for anyone who has to lead a community.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc414: Sr. A. Daria Vagni, one of the sisters of the Cento community, had died there about four months earlier, on 22 August 1868. Cf. Arch St FSA, Pos. Cento. In the dream the Mother feels the closeness and comfort of this creature born of her in the Spirit, the first Daughter of Saint Anne to pass into eternity.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc416: This letter, like the other (no. 83), was found among the papers of the superior Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni. Luigia Camisa left the Institute on 4 August 1869.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc417: Kissing the dear hand of the dear Eternal Father: an attitude of trust and abandonment to God, with whom she relates with the feelings of a child sure of its father's love. She feels that strong, powerful hand pressing on her head, yet it is sweet to her to clasp it to her breast in a burst of praise and thanksgiving for all he is doing for our good.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc418: You will call me by letter, because even in her journeys she submitted, in a spirit of obedience, to Fr. Tornatore's approval.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc420: Patience, courage...: the spirit of evil wants to do its work in the Sampierdarena house too, hindering God's plan.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc421: Courage, the ugly monster will never win again: all his efforts are useless, because Christ has conquered and set us free; our hope rests on the Lord's mercy.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc422: Wretched: etymologically, arousing compassion, deserving pity. The Mother gives the word the pejorative sense of her own littleness and misery. She not only feels humble but practises humility.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc423: Will hold you tight in the Child Jesus: in the embrace of the "King of Heaven" made little, she will obtain for her daughter the gift of the programme of life she sets out for her.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc424: To accept sufferings lovingly, in an attitude of abandonment to God, because he offers them to us as a means of salvation.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc425: A marvellous synthesis of motherly love sublimated in the love of Jesus.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc426: She is at home with her family in Genoa, for health reasons and at her parents' wish.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc427: If I were not so heavily darkened by a very dense veil!
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc432: The draft lacks the addressee's surname and the date. notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc434: Jesus gives us everything to make us feel, taste, love and be nourished by this most living love. Verbs that draw the whole creature into the mystery of a love that comes close and becomes flesh, to teach us where to find the delightful nourishment of love. It is the simple, clear language of one who has mystically experienced the love of God.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc435:
Behold: the Mother introduces her correspondent to mental prayer on the mystery of the incarnation and develops it in three points:

a) full of wonder and love, she reads the harsh reality of Bethlehem; (§3)

b) she meditates on that reality and lets it challenge her, drawing from it concrete resolutions to follow Christ in poverty, chastity and obedience; (§ 4)

c) a practical synthesis of commitment: she shows where those resolutions are to be channelled so that they become life lived: to seek only to please the Spouse Jesus (§ 5).
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc436: Humility... queen of every virtue: as the overall attitude Christ adopted in the incarnation, it is the radical condition in which our yes to God matures, which requires renouncing the evil one in order to cling to Jesus alone on the way of incarnation and self-emptying; so it is a virtue of the first importance, a valuable gem (= precious stone).
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc437: Jesus' choices, his way of poverty and meekness, contrast with human aspirations to power and to easy, brilliant achievements. We must therefore stay continually in Jesus' school, always listening to his inspirations and promptings.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc438: Gigino, the family pet name of her son Alessandro.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc440: Maddalena Patrone and Caterina Combaz, the teachers who taught without pay in the school Fr. Angelo Ricchini had opened even before the Daughters of Saint Anne arrived.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc442: An intimate relationship, overflowing with motherly love.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc443: Desire anticipates the meeting and gives a foretaste of the joy of being together.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc444: It is Jesus who is calling you, not I. His is a bridal call. How could you not hear his voice?
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc445: Now, more than ever. It is Christmas; he comes as a little child and wants to find hearts empty, because he longs to take possession of them.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc446: The language expresses the experience of a reality beyond what is humanly imaginable, a sublime and transcendent reality.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc447: To reach this, you see: experience translated into total existential choices and attitudes: a relationship with Jesus drawn from his own reality, his life, his mystery of incarnation and redemption, until one comes into his presence in the purple robe enamelled with his most divine blood.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc448: Mother Rosa's devotion to the Cross follows models inherited from the past and very much alive in her time, but she gives it the stamp of personal experience. In her little room in Piacenza she would lie down on the cross, with a living will to offer herself for her «beloved».
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc449: Love, for charity's sake. She neither knows nor can give her a more sublime exhortation, nor one with a deeper, more heartfelt intention of love.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc450: Melted: fused by the intense ardour of that Heart, a cave of blazing love.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fnc451: The Superior: Sr. A. Maria Luigia Camisa; Sr. A. Eufemia Mirisole.
